claim: Midjourney's official v6 announcement said prompting differs significantly from prior models, users must relearn how to prompt, and v6 is much more sensitive to the prompt and better at understanding you if you are explicit.
quote: Prompting with V6 is significantly different than V5. You will need to 'relearn' how to prompt. V6 is MUCH more sensitive to your prompt.

claim: Because v6 understands prompts much better, users should strip out junk quality and camera words (8k, best quality, Canon EOS R5) and be descriptive; an old keyword-laden prompt reduced to 'real photography of 21 year old chinese girl in sunlight' with nothing lost.
quote: get rid of junk like '8k, best quality'... be very descriptive about what you want, because the V6 model understands prompts much better than previous models... nothing lost by stripping out all of the camera-words and 'quality words'.

claim: v6 can take long, complex, conversational prompts and create accurate images that fulfill nearly every element, a marked upgrade over v5.2's prompt comprehension.
quote: V6 can now take long and complex prompts, and create accurate images... the model is extremely sensitive... Better prompt comprehension

claim: In token-retention testing v6 held all prompt elements through seven steps before parts started disappearing, one step further than v5.2, evidencing greater tolerance for longer prompts.
quote: V6 made it to an impressive seven steps before parts of the prompt started disappearing... V5.2 started losing tokens one step earlier.

claim: v6 shifts the prompting paradigm toward natural language: write a full descriptive sentence describing a scene to a photographer rather than stuffing comma-separated keywords as in v5.
quote: Midjourney V.6 is Arriving with A Different Image Prompting Focus on Natural Language

claim: v6 was trained to render text placed inside double quotation marks as a literal instruction, and --style raw gives a more literal, less embellished result recommended for legible lettering.
quote: The V6 model was specifically trained to recognize text enclosed in quotation marks as a literal instruction... The Raw model is more literal... for text generation, this is highly recommended as it leads to more accurate and less embellished lettering.

claim: Midjourney's official docs recommend short, simple prompts and list the elements to consider: subject, medium, environment, lighting, color, mood, and composition.
quote: Short and simple prompts typically generate the best images... Subject: Who or what?... Medium: In what form?... Environment: Where?... Lighting: What kind?... Color... Mood... Composition: How is it framed?

claim: A recommended v6 prompt order is subject, style/medium, lighting, color palette, composition, mood, then parameters, leading with the most important visual element.
quote: [subject description], [style and medium], [lighting], [color palette], [composition], [mood] --ar [ratio] --v 6.1 --style raw ... Lead with the most important visual element... The order matters — earlier terms have more weight.

claim: V6 is much more sensitive to specific wording and rewards explicit description while penalizing vague filler terms like 'award-winning', 'photorealistic', '4k' or '8k'.
quote: Midjourney V6 is much more sensitive to the specific wording of prompts. This means you need to be more explicit and avoid using vague terms like 'award-winning,' 'photorealistic,' or resolution specifications like '4k,' '8k'.

claim: A common six-component v6 recipe is style, subject, setting, composition, lighting, and details, with secondary objects/characters adding narrative layers.
quote: Style — Set the artistic tone... Subject — Describe the main focus... Setting — Establish the environment... Composition — Specify perspective, framing, and focal point... Lighting — Define the light source and mood... Details — Add specificity

claim: --stylize (--s) ranges 0-1000 with default 100; low values follow the prompt literally while high values give Midjourney more artistic freedom and may stray from the prompt.
quote: The default value for stylize is 100, and you can adjust it anywhere between 0 and 1000 with the current model versions.

claim: --chaos (--c, called Variety on the website) ranges 0-100 default 0; higher values make the four grid images more different from each other and may stick less closely to the prompt.
quote: By default chaos is set to 0... You can set the chaos value anywhere between 0 and 100, but keep in mind that higher values mean the images can be quite different and may not stick as closely to your prompt.

claim: --weird (--w) defaults to 0 and accepts values up to 3000, adding experimental/unconventional qualities; it is an experimental feature and not fully compatible with seeds.
quote: By default, weird is set to 0, but you can add values up to 3000. Keep in mind that weird is an experimental feature... Weird is also not fully compatible with seeds.

claim: --raw (Raw mode) turns off Midjourney's automatic creative styling, yielding more realistic/photo-like results from simple prompts and giving detailed prompts more control; compatible with v5.1+.
quote: When you switch to Raw, you're essentially turning off this 'auto-pilot.' With simple prompts, you'll often get more realistic, photo-like images... Raw is compatible with Midjourney versions 5.1 and later.

claim: In Midjourney, --no X is equivalent to a -0.5 multi-prompt weight (X::-0.5); negative weights are how you tell Midjourney what to exclude, and the sum of all weights must stay positive or it errors.
quote: Using the no parameter is the same as using a -0.5 weight. So vibrant tulip fields --no red is the same as vibrant tulip fields:: red::-0.5... the total of all weights in your prompt needs to be a positive number.

claim: The v5-era default parameter table lists Quality values 0.25/0.5/1 (default 1), Seed range 0-4294967295 (random default), Stop 10-100, Stylize 0-1000 default 100, Chaos 0-100, aspect ratio default 1:1.
--seed sets the starting noise for reproducibility/testing, but seeds have the least impact on the final image and Turbo mode breaks reliable seed locking.
quote: Don't use Turbo mode when using seeds. Turbo mode focuses on speed, and as a result seed locking is not reliable.

claim: --tile generates a single seamless tile whose edges match for repeating patterns (fabrics, wallpaper); upscaling tile images often breaks the seamless repeat.
quote: The --tile parameter makes sure that the edges of your image match up perfectly... upscaling your tile images will often break the seamless repeating pattern, so upscaling these images is not recommended.

claim: Quality (--q) controls how much GPU time is spent and only affects the initial four-image set, not variations, upscales or inpainting; in v7 default is 1 with 2/4 options (older models used 0.25/0.5/1).
quote: the quality parameter only influences the first set of four images you create. It doesn't affect later variations, inpainting/outpainting, or upscales.

claim: --aspect/--ar sets non-square aspect ratios (default 1:1); parameters must go at the prompt end with no space before the dashes and no punctuation.
quote: vibrant California poppies--ar 2:3 (No space before the dashes)... Midjourney images start as squares, but you can change this using the aspect ratio parameter --aspect or --ar

claim: The --no parameter is simply shorthand for a negative multi-prompt weight of ::-0.5, and negative weights are relative so wood::1 teapot::-1 behaves identically to wood::10 teapot::-10.
quote: The `--no` command is a shorthand for '`::-0.5`' which is just a regular negative weight... negative prompts are also relative, so `wood::1 teapot::-1` is the same as `wood::10 teapot::-10`.

claim: For Midjourney v6 the image-weight parameter --iw accepts a range of 0-3 with a default of 1, a wider ceiling than the 0-2 range used in earlier versions.
quote: for Midjourney Version 6 specifically: Default value: "1"; Range: "0-3"

claim: Style references are added via --sref followed by an image URL or one of Midjourney's predefined numeric sref codes (or --sref random), and --sw controls style influence on a 0-1000 scale with a default of 100, where --sw 0 cancels the --sref.
quote: add the --sref parameter to the end of your prompt, then pasting your image URL... The Style Weight parameter... ranges from 0 to 1000, with the default setting being 100. A value of --sw 0 cancels out the --sref.

claim: With --sw, values below 100 dilute the reference style to give the prompt more room while values above 100 make the referenced style dominant, and the practical sweet spot tends to fall between 65 and 175; --sref random generates a reusable numeric code shown in the prompt after generation.
quote: Lower values (below 100): gradually dilute the SREF's presence... Higher values (above 100): increase the influence of the SREF... The recommended "sweet spot" falls between 65 and 175... instead of `--sref random`, you will see `--sref <number>`

claim: Character consistency uses --cref URL pointing at a character image with --cw from 100 (default, carrying face/hair/clothes) down to 0 (face only, good for changing outfit/hair); it is precision-limited, will not reproduce exact dimples, freckles or t-shirt logos, and is not designed for real people or photos.
quote: Type `--cref URL`... strength 100 (`--cw 100`) is default... uses the face, hair, and clothes... at zero strength it'll just focus on face... it won't copy exact dimples / freckles / or tshirt logos... not designed for real people / photos

claim: V6 is more sensitive to prompt wording, advises against 'junk keywords', and requires relearning the comma-keyword style that worked in earlier versions.
quote: V6 is more sensitive to the prompt and advises against using 'junk keywords'... very short prompts like keywords with commas may not work as well in V5 as in the previous versions.

claim: Official Midjourney docs cover the --no parameter as the dedicated way to exclude elements rather than naming unwanted things in the positive prompt.
quote: The '--no' parameter explicitly tells the AI to exclude certain elements.

claim: Naming an unwanted element in a positive prompt (e.g. 'without hats') forces the model to parse a negation and can emphasize the thing instead; --no reliably removes it.
quote: It's easier for Midjourney to understand what you want than to figure out what to remove... the visual evidence shows --no hat achieved 100% hat-free results consistently.

claim: Stacking five or more style modifiers in v6 causes them to average into mush, a key reason old keyword-stacking prompts fail.
quote: Stacking 5+ style modifiers causes them to average to mush... v6, which moved away from the keyword-stacking approach that worked in earlier versions.

claim: Longer prompts make Midjourney more likely to assign weight 0.00 to important keywords, especially later in the prompt, which it then ignores.
quote: The longer your prompt is, the more likely Midjourney is to assign a weight of 0.00 to important keywords, especially later on in the prompt, which it will then ignore when making your image.

claim: High --stylize values let Midjourney take creative liberty and ignore some specified details to polish the image, washing out prompt fidelity.
quote: high --stylize (e.g., --s 750): Midjourney takes a lot more creative liberty... sometimes even ignoring a few of your specific details to do so.

claim: The /shorten command scores each token 0-1 and strikes through near-zero-weight words, exposing junk modifiers that contribute nothing to the image.
quote: the /shorten command assigns token importance ratings from 0-1, visually distinguishing high-impact words through bolding and low-impact ones through strikethrough formatting.

claim: Midjourney tokenizes prompts and begins omitting details past a token threshold; fusing words with underscores into single tokens raises per-token weight.
quote: It is the number of tokens that determines when Midjourney might start omitting details from your prompt. Joining the words together with underscores 'fuses' them into one token.

claim: Midjourney v6.1 was the default from July 30 2024 until June 16 2025, when V7 (released April 3 2025) became the default on June 17 2025.
quote: V6.1 was released on July 30, 2024, and was the default until June 16, 2025. V7 was released on April 3, 2025, and became the default on June 17, 2025.

claim: Midjourney's official V7 alpha announcement says V7 is an entirely new model that may require different styles of prompting and is much smarter with text prompts.
quote: an entirely new model with unique strengths and probably a few weaknesses ... keep in mind it may require different styles of prompting

claim: V7 improved prompt understanding by roughly 35%, so simpler prompts now produce better results than the parameter-heavy habits V6 relied on.
quote: Prompt understanding improved 35%, meaning simpler prompts now produce better results.

claim: A 2026 review notes V6 relied on parameter-heavy prompting habits while V7 achieves precision through the model itself, rewarding simpler more direct prompts and is strongest when visual taste matters as much as literal instruction following.
quote: V7 is strongest when visual taste matters as much as literal instruction following

claim: Prompting philosophies differ sharply: Midjourney uses comma-separated aesthetic phrases plus parameters, DALL-E 3 demands natural-language full sentences, Flux leverages photographic/camera terminology, and Stable Diffusion uses weighted parentheses syntax with a negative prompt field.
quote: Midjourney prioritizes aesthetic phrases, DALL·E 3 demands natural prose, Flux leverages photographic language, and Stable Diffusion relies on weighted keyword control

claim: Flux follows instructions precisely (e.g. exactly three people in specific positions) whereas Midjourney is aesthetic-first and may ignore literal specs, though v6.1 improved its understanding of intent.
quote: Flux follows instructions precisely ... Midjourney ... aesthetic-first ... You ask for a red car, get a blue one. ... V6.1 update made it way better at understanding what you actually mean

claim: By 2026 the model landscape moved on: Flux 2 family launched Nov 25 2025, GPT Image replaced DALL-E 3, and Midjourney shipped V8 with a rewritten engine and native 2K output.
quote: Flux 2 family launched on November 25, 2025, Midjourney V8 launched in March 2026 with a fully rewritten engine — 5x faster with native 2K output, and GPT Image 2 dropped in April 2026, replacing DALL-E 3
